guidance: Preliminary engineering estimate—verify loads, materials, governing standards, and calculations with a qualified engineer before fabrication or construction.
method: The bend is described by the material thickness t, the inside radius R, the bend angle A in degrees and the K-factor k, which is the share of the thickness from the inside face to the neutral axis. The angle is converted to radians, theta = A * pi / 180. The neutral-axis radius is Rn = R + k * t, the bend allowance is the arc length of the neutral axis, BA = theta * Rn, the outside setback is OSSB = (R + t) * tan(theta / 2), and the bend deduction is BD = 2 * OSSB - BA, the amount by which the flat blank is shorter than the sum of the two outside leg dimensions. For a part with two outside legs L1 and L2 the flat length is L1 + L2 - BD. Values are computed unrounded and then rounded to three decimals for display, so the deduction uses the unrounded allowance and setback. The units label applies to every length and no conversion is performed, so millimetres and inches give the same numbers for the same figures. Thickness must be 0.001 to 100, inside radius 0 to 500, bend angle 0.1 to 179.9 degrees, K-factor 0 to 0.5, and each leg 0 to 100000 in the chosen units; each leg must also be at least R + t to clear the bend, and the flat length must be greater than zero. Blank fields, text, exponent notation, negatives and out-of-range values are refused with the exact reason, and a decimal comma is accepted. An inside radius smaller than the thickness, and a bend of 165 degrees or more, produce warnings rather than refusals. The tool computes developed length from the K-factor you supply: it does not choose tooling, a minimum bend radius, springback compensation or a material-specific K-factor, and it does not check whether the finished part is strong enough for its job. It runs entirely in the browser with no storage, uploads or network access.

sources.title: The neutral axis of a bent sheet sits part-way through the thickness, at the inside radius plus the K-factor times the thickness.
The bend allowance is the arc length of the neutral axis over the bend angle, and the outside setback is (R + t) times the tangent of half the bend angle.
The bend deduction is twice the outside setback minus the bend allowance, so a part with two outside legs has a flat length of both legs minus one bend deduction.
